messages:
maria: Heads-up — getting a cluster of 503s for hosted inference across us-west-2 over the last ~10m. Customer support flagged 3 customers. Error pattern looks like gateway 503 then client timeouts. throwing this into triage.
aj: Seeing the same. Grafana: spike in gateway 5xx, inference runtime error rate up ~4% for p50>2000ms requests. Link: https://grafana.internal/r/hosted/503s
sam: Any deploys in that window? infra-bot: deploy-bot just posted: 
```
[deploy-bot] 2026-02-18T12:30:02Z - service/hosted-gateway v2.14.1 -> canary
canary started: 12:31:10Z
```
maria: Canary started ~2m before the spike. Can we confirm rolling vs full? aj: Canary only for 10% of traffic. But metrics show broader impact so either traffic routing or a downstream cascade.
ops-oncall: Repro attempt — curl against hosted endpoint returns 503 consistently for a small batch. Here's quick repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx" 
  -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"test"}' -v
* HTTP/2 503
* Received HTTP code 503 from server
```
sam: Error logs from gateway show: `upstream: connection reset by peer` and repeated `504 read timeout from backend` in same timeframe. Posting trimmed log sample:
```
[hosted-gateway] 2026-02-18T12:32:05Z ERROR upstream request failed: dial tcp 10.4.12.90:8080: connect: connection refused
[hosted-runtime] 2026-02-18T12:32:06Z WARN kvcache: miss spike, mem pressure 78%
```
aj: mem pressure + connection reset suggests runtime workers OOM/crash or transient network flapping to runner pool. Sam can you check node-level evictions and pod restarts?
sam: Checking now — saw a few kube OOMKilled on runners in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 around 12:31-12:33Z. Also autoscaler didn't react instantly because CPU thresholds weren't hit (KV cache spike caused mem but not CPU). We might have had a resource config gap on quantized models -> memory spike.
maria: Mitigation suggestion: 1) scale up runner pool capacity in affected regions 2) temporarily route heavy customers to fallback smaller model (rw-medium-quant) 3) enable 30s increased backend timeout in gateway for in-flight requests 4) rollback canary if linked.
ops-oncall: Started scaling runners + triggered emergency routing rule to fallback model for top 3 affected tenants. Applied for 15m. aj: I enabled increased gateway backend timeout to 30s for canary group.
infra-bot: autoscaler: manual scale-up initiated: +12 runners in us-west-2, +8 runners in eu-west-1. Expected ready ~2m.
support-bot: Notifying affected customers via support channel and creating ticket INC-20260218-503. Customers: AcmePay, Learnspark, Docflow. Customers reported API timeouts and failed webhooks.
maria: Action items while we stabilize: - sam to collect full runtime core dumps and container logs (sam) - aj to isolate canary traffic and produce timeline + deploy diff (aj) - support to compile list of impacted requests and refunds policy (support-bot) - ops to run post-incident runbook and coordinate postmortem (ops-oncall)
sam: Collected logs and a couple of core dumps; pushing to /artifacts/INC-20260218-503/logs.tar.gz. Preliminary find: memory usage trend shows KV cache thrash after canary introduced larger sequence-length samples in Canary model config.
aj: Deploy diff shows a change in model serving config: `max_sequence_length` increased for canary variant which accidentally enabled larger kv cache allocation per request. Rolling rollback of canary in progress.
ops-oncall: Canary rollback completed at 12:45Z. 5xx trend falling back to baseline ~12:47Z. Need to monitor for recurrence. ops-oncall: scaling completed; runners stabilized.
maria: Thanks — sounds like root cause is canary config change that increased memory per request causing OOMs under real traffic, leading to gateway 503s. Postmortem items: 1) Add pre-canary load-simulation for config changes that affect per-request memory 2) Add alert for KV cache miss/spike tied to memory pressure 3) Tighten autoscaler to account for memory+io, not just CPU 4) Update runbook for immediate fallback routing and automated model downgrade rule 5) Support: standard customer credit playbook for transient infra 503s.
aj: I'll own remediation item 1 and 3. sam will own logs and fix for detecting per-request memory spike. support-bot: I'll prepare customer comms template and escalation notes.
maria: Let's plan a 30-minute postmortem tomorrow and include runtime, infra, product (model config), and support. Assigning owners in incident doc INC-20260218-503. Please add any further observations here. :white_check_mark:
support-bot: Ticket INC-20260218-503 updated: postmortem scheduled 2026-02-19T16:00Z. Notifying customers and CSMs. :email:
maria: Closing triage thread for now — monitoring. If 503s reappear reopen and escalate. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
